course:
Lectures are quite hard to digest and learn in one go if you don't have a background close to the field. Notes and writing part doesn't invoke learning. In lessons we talk about practical applications(which is helpful and couldn't be found in a book) but exams are almost fully theoretical. Homeworks are assessed in an unfair way. There isn't a satisfactory answer to the problems given in homeworks but rather the longest answer is given full credits and other answers are scaled to with respect to that. So if you wrote a half page paragraph that is enough to answer the question but one of your peers wrote two pages, you get 25%. This is very demotivating. I don't think assessment procedures in this course is very effective in promoting learning. Unfortunately, it seems that it is just there to scale and give you a grade. 
This is also present in the midterm examination. One of the questions in midterm was to calculate an iterative method(with calculator) for two iterations. Even though it is a mechanical process and rather straightforward, it is very easy to do a mistake and lose 25% percent from your exam grade. That type of question measures how good of a MATLAB you are which is contradicting to the paradigm of academia in an age where innovation and critical thinking is expected from a researcher/student.

Weakest: the course syllabus is too much for a regular "Advanced Numerical Methods" course in comparison to the courses presented in many top universities worldwide. "Finite Element Methods" and "Numerical Solutions for Partial Differential Equations" can be presented in separate courses (based on the need of the students of any field). Presenting too much stuff in this course, without any step-by-step example solving in the class, results in great pressure on students and disrupts their mind integrity of the subjects.

The course covers a lot of fundamental topics in numerical methods and gives us a nice and solid background. Coding homeworks are very educative, but some are very long and the reporting becomes too cumbersome when we have to do the same thing several times in a single question (and to do this for all questions). The class can sometimes get too cumbersome, when it is only made up of us copying equations from the board. More explanations during the derivations would be nice (so that it would differ more from us just reading the derivation from the book).
One can learn a great deal about programming specially students from natural sciences.
